body:
## Feature Summary

Cut the start-up context that every Claude Code session on this fleet pays before its first answer. Five ranked parts were measured and brainstormed one by one. A low-risk set of changes saves about 2.4 percent of the whole token bill; a second, owner-gated set saves a further 3.6 percent (5.99 percent in total, not the sum of the per-part figures because the parts overlap).

## Problem Statement

Measured on 2026-11-24 over all 12,753 Claude Code transcripts on this host (2,177 main sessions, 10,576 subagent sessions, 299,350 real turns, 12.4 billion cost units): a session carries a median of about 75,000 tokens of start-up context (10th percentile 28,383, 90th 99,498) before it does any work, and the median session lasts only 9 turns. The start-up context is **26.3 percent of the whole bill** (28.1 percent in subagent sessions). Every 10,000 tokens removed saves about 3.6 percent of the bill. The bill that counts is every work session in every worktree, not the coordinator.

Breakdown of the start-up context (Claude models count 2.72 characters per token, other models about 4.5, so the same text is 1.5 to 1.7 times larger on Claude). The five largest parts we can change, by fleet mean tokens per session (share of the whole bill if the part were removed entirely, a ceiling and not a plan):

| Rank | Part | Mean tokens | Bill share | Owner of the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Artifact tools (Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData; harness-added, median 16,219 tokens where present; only 4 direct publishes in 27 days, all from main sessions) | 7,912 | 3.15% | harness; agent frontmatter and a settings switch |
| 2 | Project `CLAUDE.md` (27,339 characters, loaded whole in 8,450 sessions) | 6,521 | 2.15% | this repo |
| 3 | Our skills and commands listing entries (capped by the harness at about 30,000 characters) | 4,952 | 1.85% | settings |
| 4 | User `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and the Bash inspection policy that subagents receive twice | 4,805 | 1.61% | this repo, installed template |
| 5 | Custom agent prompt bodies (subagents only; includes a 13,100-character memory block added to six agents that never use it) | 4,478 | 1.83% | this repo |

Other sizable parts, not part of this issue: Playwright plugin tools 1.46 percent, Pragmatic output style 1.55 percent, built-in core tools 1.26 percent (harness-fixed).

## User Story

As the owner paying for the fleet, I want the start-up context of every session trimmed where it can be done with little or no behavior risk, so that the same work costs fewer tokens, and so that each cut is test-pinned and can be rolled back.

## Proposed Solution

Preference stated by the owner: spend more tokens if that means less risk. So the plan is two sets. Nothing in the first set removes a rule, a tool a session needs, or a reviewer's input.

**SAFE set (about 2.38 percent of the bill; 1.99 percent if the next install of the core `CLAUDE.md` is untrimmed):**

1. Tests first: one table-driven `tests/agents/test_agent_frontmatter_policy.py` (accepts a superset in `disallowedTools`, pins agent bodies by hash in the PR diff, keeps the four existing agent-roster tests) and `tests/core/test_project_claude_md_absolute_rules.py` (sha256 pins of the five ABSOLUTE RULE sections plus the worktree section, key-phrase checks, a size ratchet).
2. One combined agent-frontmatter change in this order: (a) delete `memory: project` from `rf-qa`, `rf-qa-qualitative`, `rf-analyst`, `rf-assembler`, `rf-team-lead`, `rf-task-executor` (keep it on `rf-task-builder` and `rf-task-researcher`, the only agents that ever wrote memory); (b) ONE merged `disallowedTools` line on the 20 agents that have no `tools:` allowlist, Artifact trio first (`Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData`), and `Skill` added only after a live first-request check and never on `debate-orchestrator`, `merge-executor` or `quality-engineer`.
3. Trim the project `CLAUDE.md` in two stages with every rule untouched: stage 1 removes 7,400 characters (Core Architecture, Testing with PM Agent, Core Development Principles, MCP Server Integration, Development & Installation, Package Information, the "Required Commands" block, the plugin-system note) and archives them verbatim in `docs/developer-guide/technical-architecture.md`; stage 2 condenses a further 2,500 characters (Project Structure, Development Workflow, Plugin Override).
4. Lower the skills-listing cap with `"skillListingBudgetFraction": 0.006` in the tracked `.claude/settings.json` (IronClaude checkouts only), after a pilot in an untracked `.claude/settings.local.json` or with `claude --settings` shows the listing block falls from about 30,025 to about 18,000 characters (accept 17,000 to 19,000) with every skill name still listed. Descriptions of the 22 skills are not rewritten and `skillListingMaxDescChars` is not used; hiding flags are rejected.
5. Stop sending the Bash inspection policy twice to subagents: `freshness-subagent-start.sh` reads `agent_type` and skips its copy only when every condition holds (type is `general-purpose` or has an installed agent file; no `omitClaudeMd: true`; not Explore or Plan; `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` contains the exact import line; the policy file is readable). Any doubt prints the full copy as today. Then trim the codegraph paragraph of `src/superclaude/core/CLAUDE.md` (about 560 bytes kept, `pgrep` warning kept) before the next install.

**GATED set (owner decision and a live test first; a further 3.61 percent):**

6. `"enableArtifact": false` at user level (after a disposable-session test; 2.91 percent after step 2b).
7. `omitClaudeMd: true` on read-only reviewers, Tier 1 (`confidence-calibrator`, `implement-retry-adviser`, `audit-scanner`, `audit-validator`, `audit-analyzer`, `audit-comparator`: 0.14 percent) after a proof run, Tier 2 (`evidence-validator`, `reflect-reviewer`, `troubleshoot-analyst`, `reuse-auditor`: 0.29 percent) only after the seeded-defect A/B below. Both tiers keep the hook's policy copy.
8. Narrow the allowlists of `rf-qa`, `rf-qa-qualitative`, `rf-analyst` (drop `Skill`, later `Agent`, `Team*`): 0.34 percent.

Full per-part positions, risk registers, cross-examination outcomes, the union calculation and the owner questions are in the sections below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/agents/test_agent_frontmatter_policy.py` and `tests/core/test_project_claude_md_absolute_rules.py` exist and pass; the four existing agent-roster tests still pass unchanged.
- [ ] A disposable subagent's first request (in its transcript) shows the three Artifact tools absent for the 20 agents and still present for a general-purpose subagent.
- [ ] The six rf agents have no `memory: project` line; `git diff -U0` shows exactly six deleted lines; rf-qa's system prompt falls by about 13,100 characters.
- [ ] The project `CLAUDE.md` median falls from about 27,270 to about 20,000 characters (stage 1) and about 17,400 (stage 2); the hash test passes; the archive contains the removed text.
- [ ] The cap pilot proves the listing block is 17,000 to 19,000 characters, every skill and command name is listed, `/sc:brainstorm` loads its protocol, and start-up tokens fall by about 4,000 on a Claude model; only then is the key committed.
- [ ] The hook prints one policy copy for listed agent types and the full copy for Explore, Plan, `omitClaudeMd` agents, unknown types, missing `agent_type` and malformed JSON.
- [ ] After release, re-running the measurement scripts on later sessions shows the fleet bill falling by 1.99 to 2.38 percent (SAFE set), with no rise in these regression counts: `git add -f` on `.claude`, `gh pr create` without `--repo`, `git worktree add`, `orca worktree create` without `--agent`, hardcoded `src/superclaude` paths.
- [ ] Each gated item ships only after its stated proof and an owner "yes" in chat.

## Out of Scope

Rewriting ABSOLUTE RULE prose; nested `CLAUDE.md` files for rules; the Playwright plugin, the Pragmatic output style and the `pragmatic-subagent.js` and Ponytail hook texts (kept out of this release); RTK and Headroom (measured at 0.07 to 0.45 percent with cache risk, not recommended); whole-conversation cache re-writes (about 3.1 percent, cause unknown, a separate read-only investigation); shorter model output; rewriting the 22 skill descriptions; any harness-fixed part.

## Components Affected (from `/sc:analyze`)

- `src/superclaude/agents/*.md` (20 agents with no `tools:`; six rf agents with `memory: project`) and the mirror `plugins/superclaude/agents/`
- `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/CLAUDE.md` (project file, 27,339 characters) and `docs/developer-guide/technical-architecture.md` (archive)
- `.claude/settings.json` (tracked; the only tracked file under `.claude/`)
- `src/superclaude/hooks/scripts/freshness-subagent-start.sh` and `tests/hooks/test_freshness_subagent_start_policy.py`
- `src/superclaude/core/CLAUDE.md` and `src/superclaude/core/BASH_INSPECTION_POLICY.md`
- New tests: `tests/agents/test_agent_frontmatter_policy.py`, `tests/core/test_project_claude_md_absolute_rules.py`, `tests/skills/test_listing_invocability.py`
- Existing tests that read these files: `tests/agents/test_tavily_tool_parity.py`, `test_codegraph_rosters`, `test_workflow_reviser_readonly`, `tests/cli/reflect/test_reviewer_readonly_tools`, `test_issue_worker_agents`, `tests/unit/test_cli_install.py`, `tests/core/test_claude_md_worktree_rule.py`

## Related Issues/PRs

- #757 (the issue whose brainstorm produced these measurements: run the sweep outside the coordinator session and wake it only on change).
- #766 (bug: read workers show as "could not determine"; found during the same measurements, no code overlap).
- #767 (coordinator compacts its conversation too often; adjacent token-cost problem, not a duplicate).
- #575 and #580 (closed: evaluation of Bash output pruners; the RTK and Headroom comparison in the findings reaches the same conclusion on fleet data).
- No existing issue is about trimming the start-up context (searches: "startup token", "token cost", "CLAUDE.md size").

## Priority

Medium: a planned feature with a measured saving of about 2.4 percent of the bill (SAFE set), no data loss and no broken gate (Priority rule set, Medium trigger "a planned feature").

## Fix approach

Repo: IronbellyOrg/IronClaude. Base branch: master (rebase onto `origin/master` before pushing; the PR is opened with `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3`, which targets the fork only).

Commands, in order: `/sc:workflow` on this issue, then `/sc:implement` per PR below, then `/sc:pr-submit --monitor 3 --head <branch> --title "..." --body "..."` for each. Edit under `src/superclaude/` and run `make sync-dev` and `make verify-sync`; never stage `.claude/` mirrors (only `.claude/settings.json` is tracked).

Steps, in order:

- Step 1 (PR 1, tests only): add the two new test files; confirm the existing agent tests pass.
- Step 2 (PR 2, combined agent frontmatter): delete `memory: project` on six rf agents; add one merged `disallowedTools` line on the 20 no-tools agents (Artifact trio now; `Skill` after the live first-request check); mirror in `plugins/superclaude/agents/`. Gate: a disposable subagent shows the tools gone.
- Step 3 (PR 3, project `CLAUDE.md` stage 1): move 7,400 characters verbatim to the archive doc with one pointer line.
- Step 4 (PR 4, stage 2): condense 2,500 more characters.
- Step 5 (PR 5, hook and core file): the `agent_type` hook change with tests, plus the codegraph paragraph trim; ships through the Coder template (owner decision 7).
- Step 6 (pilot, then PR 6): run the cap pilot in a disposable session; commit `skillListingBudgetFraction` to `.claude/settings.json` only on a pass.
- Step 7 (gated, one at a time, each on an owner "yes"): `enableArtifact:false` after its live test; `omitClaudeMd` Tier 1 after its proof run, Tier 2 after the A/B; rf allowlist narrowing.
- Rollback for every step: `git revert`, `make sync-dev`, reinstall; the cap is reverted by deleting the key (live reload); `enableArtifact` by deleting the key or the `/config` Artifacts row.

## Test plan

- Tests to add or change: the three new test files listed under Components Affected; extend `tests/hooks/test_freshness_subagent_start_policy.py` (general-purpose with and without the import, `omitClaudeMd: true`, Explore, Plan, unknown type, missing `agent_type`, malformed JSON, `pgrep` warning kept). Seeded-defect A/B for Tier 2 reviewers and rf-qa (design in the rank 5 section below: 7 agents, 13 runs each, 91 runs, about 15 million cost units, never Opus).
- Regression gate: `uv run pytest tests/core tests/skills tests/agents tests/hooks tests/audit tests/cli/reflect tests/unit/test_cli_install.py -q`, then the full `uv run pytest`, `make lint`, `make verify-sync`.
- How a reviewer verifies: run the hash test; `git diff -U0` on agent files shows only frontmatter lines; for each gate read the first request in a disposable session's transcript (tools absent, listing block length, one policy copy); after release re-run `s8_detail.py`, `agent_cost3.py`, `recent.py` and compare against the baseline numbers in the findings below.


## Findings and recommendations (full text)

Everything below was measured or produced on 2026-11-24 from `.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/` in the Coordinator checkout (scripts rerunnable; only sizes and counts were read, never message text). Each part was brainstormed by one agent (proposal, cross-examination by the other four, final position). The five agents agreed on nine joint points (S1 to S9: one table-driven frontmatter test; one combined frontmatter change in a fixed order; corrected reach of our agent files; cap pilot scope; `evidence-validator` as Tier 2; hook fallback to full copy; settings keys kept in separate commits; install trim; figures not additive).

<details>
<summary>1. How the bill was measured (fleet of 12,753 sessions)</summary>

Date 2026-11-24. Owner correction: the bill that matters is every work session in every worktree, not the coordinator. VERDICT.md used two coordinator sessions and also counted usage twice. This file redoes the measurement on all 12,753 transcripts (25.55 GB, 474 project folders, 2,177 main sessions and 10,576 subagent sessions). Method: `m8_all_sessions.py` and `m9_startup_and_reads.py` in this folder; results `m8-all-sessions.json`, `m8-all-sessions.json.perfile.jsonl`, `m9-startup-reads.json`. Only counts were read; no message text was stored. Usage is de-duplicated by message id. Cost weights (an assumption): fresh input 1.0, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, output 5.0 (UNVERIFIED for our gateway; one-hour cache writes may cost 2.0, which would make start-up context and re-writes matter more).

## What was wrong in VERDICT.md

1. Wrong population: two coordinator sessions, which are long (thousands of turns). The fleet is mostly short sessions: 9,187 sessions under 20 turns and 3,303 between 20 and 100 turns carry 58% of the cost.
2. Double counting: one model response is written as several transcript lines that repeat its usage. On the Coder coordinator session the corrected figures are 3,618 turns (not 5,960), 1.52 billion cache-read tokens (not 2.38 billion) and 202 million units (not 334 million). Everything in VERDICT.md that used turn counts, R, the "75 whole-conversation re-writes" and the "14%" figure is retracted.

## The fleet, measured

| | All sessions | Main sessions | Subagent sessions |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sessions | 12,753 | 2,177 | 10,576 |
| Real turns | 299,350 | 116,883 | 182,467 |
| Cost units | 12,438 million | 5,791 million | 6,647 million |
| Cache reads | 58.6% | 70.2% | 48.4% |
| Cache writes | 21.8% | 16.2% | 26.7% |
| Fresh input | 4.3% | 4.1% | 4.5% |
| Output | 15.3% | 9.4% | 20.4% |
| Tool output, tokens | 550 million (4.4% of units, before re-reads) | 113 million | 437 million |
| Share: Read tool / Bash / Grep | 77.8% / 13.2% / 4.6% | 66.2% / 23.4% / 2.2% | 80.8% / 10.6% / 5.2% |
| Later turns that re-read a tool-output token (R) | Bash 32, Read 22 | Bash 48, Read 36 | Bash 23, Read 19 |

Start-up context (what a session carries before its first answer), `m9`: median 75,296 tokens (10th percentile 28,383, 90th 99,498). Median session length is 9 turns. The start-up context accounts for **26.3% of the whole bill** (28.1% in subagent sessions). Repeated reads of the same file are only 1.5% of Read output; reads over 20,000 tokens are 2.4%.

## RTK and Headroom on the fleet

- RTK acts on Bash output only. A removed token is worth 1.25 + 0.1 × R units. For the commands I could classify as filterable (`git`, `gh`, test runners, `ls`, `find`, `grep`, builds): 25.2 million tokens (4.6% of tool output), R = 26.9, value 3.94 units per token. The classification is crude (compound commands hide some), so this pool may be undercounted.
- Savings at the removal rates both advocates used: 9% = 8.9 million units (**0.07%**); 25% = 24.8 million (**0.20%**); 56% = 55.6 million (**0.45%**).
- Hard ceiling: deleting every byte of Bash output in every session saves 72.6 million tokens × 4.45 = 323 million units (**2.6%**).
- Cost side: the average turn costs 41,500 units. The middle-case saving is cancelled by 600 extra turns in 299,350 (0.2%). The independent studies measured turn increases of more than that (+13.8% in one).
- Headroom compresses the same Bash pool, skips Read results by default, and protects code. The same 0.1 to 0.5% applies. Each cache bust it may cause costs about one start-up context (about 75,000 tokens x 1.15 = 86,000 units), so 290 busts across 12,753 sessions (2.3%) cancel the middle case.
- Verdict: unchanged. Neither is worth adopting; on the fleet the best case is 0.45% and the ceiling 2.6%.

</details>

<details>
<summary>2. Start-up context: method, summary and ranked table of every part</summary>

Date 2026-11-24. Issue 757, worker brainstorm, part "startup-trim". Read-only analysis; only sizes were stored, never message text. Scripts and raw numbers: `/home/coder/workspaces/worktrees/IronClaude/Coordinator/.dev/issues/757/worker-brainstorm/startup-trim/scripts/`.

## Summary

- The earlier "about 50,000 unmeasured tokens" is now measured. Every transcript written by Claude Code 2.1.x on this host stores the full first request: the system prompt, every tool definition and every message block (`api-request-shape`, `api-request-blob`, `api-request` entries). Splitting that request by character count and converting with a per-model ratio reproduces the measured start-up tokens of each session to within about 1,000 tokens (median error 4 tokens; see Reconciliation).
- The largest single part is a group of three harness tools almost nobody uses: `Artifact`, `ArtifactComments` and `ArtifactData` (median 16,219 tokens per session where present; fleet mean 7,912 per session; 3.15 percent of the whole bill). They were called at most 8 times in at most 817,542 tool calls.
- The five largest parts we can change are: the Artifact tools (by a deny rule, UNVERIFIED that it removes them), the IronClaude project `CLAUDE.md`, our entries in the skills listing, the user `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, and our custom agent prompt bodies. Together they average 28,668 tokens per session and are 10.6 percent of the bill if removed entirely (a ceiling, not a plan: none of them can go to zero).
- Harness-fixed parts (built-in tools, built-in skills listing, system prompt, context blocks) average about 17,100 tokens per session; the built-in tools alone are 13,425 tokens and 5.9 percent of the bill.
- Token counts depend heavily on the model: Claude models use 2.72 characters per token, GPT-family models 4.6. The same start-up context is 120,662 tokens (median) in a Claude main session and 70,585 in a non-Claude main session.

## Method

1. Population. All 12,757 transcript files under `~/.claude/projects` (2,134 main and 9,599 subagent sessions usable; 998 older files have no stored request and 26 have no usage, so they are left out). A second, "recent" set is the 573 files modified in the last 3 days (396 main, 174 subagent usable). Agent type comes from each subagent's `.meta.json`.
2. Start-up tokens of a session = `input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens` of its first assistant response. The request that produced it is found through the response's `requestRef`, then resolved to its `shape` (system blocks and tools) and its `tail` (message blobs).
3. Parts. Tools are measured as compact JSON (`name`, `description`, `input_schema`) and grouped by built-in name or MCP server. Message text is split by fixed markers: the instructions reminder is split per `Contents of <path>` file; the harness's system-role message is split at hook headers (`SessionStart`, `SubagentStart`, `UserPromptSubmit`), `# Environment`, `# Output Style:`, `Available agent types`, `# MCP Server Instructions` and `The following skills are available`. Skill and agent listings are split per entry and grouped by where the entry comes from (our skills and commands, BMad, plugins, harness built-ins). For custom subagents, the system prompt is split into the harness header and the agent's own body.
4. Characters to tokens. One ratio per model, measured on all sessions of that model (`s7-calibration-all.json`): the median of (characters in the request) / (start-up tokens). A least-squares fit with separate ratios for tool definitions and for text confirms it (Claude Sonnet, 5,011 sessions: 2.758 characters per token for tools, 2.805 for text, median error 0.46 percent).
5. Bill share. As in `m9`: a session's start-up cost = fresh + 1.25 x cache write + 0.1 x cache read of the first response + 0.1 x start-up tokens x (turns - 1). Each part gets the fraction of that cost equal to its share of the start-up tokens. Weights fresh 1.0, cache write 1.25, cache read 0.1, output 5.0 are the same assumption as VERDICT-2 (UNVERIFIED for our gateway). The total bill in this population is 11,116 million units; the start-up prefix is 26.69 percent of it (VERDICT-2 measured 26.3 percent on a slightly larger population).
6. Disk side (sizes and names only): `s9_disk.py`, `s14_verify.py`. Tool use counts: one `rg` pass over all transcripts (`s15-tool-use-counts.txt`).
